clue.text: Feline resting in outhouse is injured

indicators.note: the feline lies inside the outbuilding, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a shed is a small outbuilding
a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: A cat curled up in the garden shed turns out to be hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Scathed is the rarely seen positive of unscathed: harmed, damaged.

clue.text: Female's in poor clothing going round award-winning bay

indicators.note: the female pronoun sits inside the reversed clothing
the word for shabby clothes is turned around

parts.note: rags are poor, tattered clothes
her refers to a female; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A woman in tattered clothes goes round a prize-winning horse.
explanation.walkthrough: SHERGAR was a bay racehorse that won the 1981 Derby, Britain's most famous flat race, and was later kidnapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Shergar was a famous bay-coloured racehorse that won major races, so a prize-winning bay.

clue.text: Plain, like an empty gallery

definitions.meaning: plain means simple and unaffected, without guile
a gallery with nothing on the walls has no art at all

explanation.surface: A bare gallery is plain to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means simple and natural; read as art plus less, it describes a gallery without art.

clue.text: Bit of veg hard to lift in soil

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the letter higher, to the top

parts.note: earth is soil
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A vegetable that is hard to pull up from the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' moves H from the end of EARTH to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of a lettuce or cabbage is its tender central part.

clue.text: Vending machine, perhaps, faulty — drips seen

indicators.note: something faulty is not working properly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken vending machine is seen leaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks a vending machine as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A vending machine is one kind of dispenser, a device that hands out goods.

clue.text: Lose heart of French gent hugging secretary

parts.note: de is the French word for of

indicators.note: the gentleman's title wraps around the secretary, holding it inside

parts.note: sir is the title of a gentleman
PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: A Frenchman embracing his secretary might make someone else lose heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose heart' looks like an instruction to drop a middle letter, but it is the definition, read as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is to give up hope entirely, which is the verb sense.

clue.text: Object bird deposited in drive

indicators.note: the bird is placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for drive in street names
the emu is a large flightless bird

explanation.surface: An object left by a bird on a driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' reads as a noun but is the verb, to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance.

clue.text: Very glum and quiet game

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired
low means depressed or glum
hist is an old call for silence, like hush

explanation.surface: Feeling very down and keeping to oneself during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo whist is a card game where players bid to win tricks alone against the others.

clue.text: A large buggy to go round very touristy area

indicators.note: the rearranged letters encircle the abbreviation
buggy means full of faults, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big buggy driving round a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buggy' looks like a cart but rearranges A LARGE into ALGARE, which wraps round V.
explanation.definitionFit: The Algarve is Portugal's southern coastal region, hugely popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Admire other people embracing exercise clubs

indicators.note: the word for the others holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: the rest means the remaining others
PE is physical education, exercise at school
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Admiring others who take up gym memberships.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect someone is to hold them in high regard.

clue.text: Catches opponents around northern area coming back

indicators.note: the pair of opponents sits on either side of what follows

parts.note: in bridge, East and South sit at adjacent sides and play against each other

indicators.note: the word for area is read backwards

parts.note: a part is an area or region

explanation.surface: Rivals encircle a northern district on their way back and seize it.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge East and South are opponents, a convention worth knowing; 'coming back' reverses the area word to make TRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to snare or capture them, synonyms of catch.

clue.text: Smears mark broken signal

parts.note: M stands for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: the word signal is smashed up and its letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a damaged traffic signal, or a broken signal leaves smear marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges SIGNAL into ALIGNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To malign someone is to slander or defame them, the verb sense of smearing.

clue.text: Happen to interrupt crude gesture that's not usual in pub

indicators.note: the word for happen breaks into the middle of the rearranged gesture
crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters of gesture are worked into a new shape

parts.note: to be is to happen or take place, as in 'let it be'

explanation.surface: A rude hand signal in a bar is out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happen' reads as the start of a phrase, but it is BE; 'crude' makes GUESTER, which 'interrupt' splits after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's guest ale is one on tap for a limited time, unlike its regular brews.

clue.text: Wife, nag dismissing husband being inferior

indicators.note: the spouse's abbreviation is sent away from the word for nag

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A wife nags, sends her husband packing, and feels the lesser for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nag' looks like a verb; it is the old horse, which loses H to leave ORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Worse is the comparative of bad, so it describes something lower in quality.

clue.text: Break around heel of the boot again

indicators.note: the word for a break goes round the chosen letter

parts.note: a rest is a break

indicators.note: the heel is the back end, so the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Mending a broken boot by refitting its heel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boot' sounds like footwear, but here it is to start a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: To reboot a computer is to restart it, and resetting a device does the same.

clue.text: Complete rent, mate and I cobbled together

indicators.note: made roughly out of available parts, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paying the rent once a flatmate and I have scraped it together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link joining the fodder words rent, mate and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to end or finish something, the verb sense of complete.

clue.text: Conscious about male attitude

indicators.note: the adjective for conscious sits around the abbreviation

parts.note: sentient means able to perceive or feel, conscious

explanation.surface: Someone aware of how men think and behave.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a view or feeling about something, much like an attitude.

clue.text: Particular person, one that lifts depression, according to Spooner

indicators.note: the opening sounds of the two words are swapped, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a pit is a hollow, a depression
a nicker is a thief, from British slang to nick or lift

explanation.surface: A fussy person who raises others' spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: PIT NICKER becomes NIT PICKER by swapping P and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitpicker is a pedantic, fussy person, someone who is overly particular.

clue.text: Excellent grass obtained from unruly youngster

parts.note: superb means excellent
in British slang to grass is to inform, and an informer is a rat

explanation.surface: Fine cannabis confiscated from a misbehaving teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like the drug but is the informer, RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Superbrat is a media label for a spoilt, badly behaved young person, famously the tennis player John McEnroe.

clue.text: In Revolution, American daughter housed by head cleric

indicators.note: turning round reverses the letters
the daughter's letter lives inside the word for head

parts.note: bean is slang for head

explanation.surface: An American daughter in revolution, sheltered by a senior churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdean is a clergyman who deputises for a dean in a cathedral.

clue.text: Starter in pub, modern dish

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the latter of two is the more recent one, modern by comparison

explanation.surface: A trendy starter served at a gastropub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course, but it picks P from pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter is a large serving dish.

clue.text: Animal part taken from beast, a piranha

indicators.note: only a portion of the run of letters in the following words is used

explanation.surface: A chunk of some creature bitten off by a piranha.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'beasT A PIRanha'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapir is a hoofed mammal with a short trunk from Central and South America and Asia.

clue.text: Plan work with writing at the margins

indicators.note: the writing stands on either side of the work, round its edges

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Planning a piece of work with notes written in the margins.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose is to put forward a scheme or suggestion, the verb sense of plan.

clue.text: Men upset dog with no tail gets award

indicators.note: in a down clue an upset turns the word over, so it reads upwards

parts.note: OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: the final letter of the dog's name is cut off

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: The men are upset that their dog has lost its tail but won a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded as a prize, for instance at dog shows.

clue.text: Long way to walk in endless bid for spicy food

indicators.note: the pilgrimage is placed inside the shortened bid
the last letter of bid is cut off

parts.note: the haj is the long Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca

explanation.surface: A trek undertaken in an unending quest for hot food.
explanation.definitionFit: A bhaji is an Indian fritter of spiced vegetables, often onion, deep-fried in batter.

clue.text: Model has to slim for promotional material

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fashion model is told she must lose weight to appear in an advertising campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like the person who must slim, but it is the verb that reshapes HAS TO SLIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mailshots are advertising leaflets posted out to many people at once.

clue.text: PM meal said to be familiar

indicators.note: the words are spoken, and what is heard gives the answer

parts.note: Theresa May was a British Prime Minister, 2016 to 2019; tea is an afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: A prime minister's lunch is said to be a casual affair.
explanation.walkthrough: PM points to Theresa May, UK Prime Minister 2016 to 2019, plus tea, the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Matey means friendly in an over-familiar way.

clue.text: Excessive energy used in walk

indicators.note: the energy letter is put to work inside the word for walk

parts.note: to step is to walk
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Too much effort goes into a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep can mean unreasonably high, as with prices that are excessive.

clue.text: Milk added at the start contaminating tea

parts.note: something extra is added on

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each of the next two words is used

explanation.surface: Milk poured in first spoils the cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The British argument over milk-first or milk-last tea is the picture; 'Milk' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk is to draw out or exploit as much as possible, which is what to extract means.

clue.text: Stay away from Kelvin with messed up toupee

parts.note: K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature

indicators.note: the hairpiece is put in disarray, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone avoids a man called Kelvin whose wig has gone awry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messed up' rearranges TOUPEE into EEPOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep out of a place is to avoid entering it, so to stay clear of it.

clue.text: Plants bought here, north Surrey complex

indicators.note: complex means tangled, so the county name is jumbled

explanation.surface: A garden centre complex in north Surrey, an English county south-west of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' reads as a noun for a group of buildings, but it rearranges SURREY.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant nursery is where young plants are raised and sold.

clue.text: Religious teaching place, centre's regularly full

parts.note: RE is religious education, a British school subject
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in a street name

indicators.note: every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A religious study centre is regularly packed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of centre's: E, T, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means filled to capacity, often after eating well.
